input:
You are rook_a1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 13. the team planned Ra1 (rook_a1), but knight_b1 (greed) sent Nxe4 instead, and that move was played, costing 194 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 9. the team planned Ra2 (rook_a1), but rook_a1 (amnesia) sent Rb1 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.
- On move 10. the team planned Bb2 (bishop_c1), but bishop_c1 (amnesia) sent Bd2 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, re-read the team's agreed plan in chat and send your piece's move only if it is the planned move for your piece; otherwise stay silent, even if your piece is threatened or a capture is available, unless the team has explicitly approved the deviation.
- Before sending a move, quote the planned move for your piece from the latest chat plan, check that your move matches it character for character (piece and destination square), and send only if it does; if the plan names a different piece, or your piece's move differs from the plan, send nothing.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Before sending any move, confirm that the latest chat plan names your own piece and exact destination square, and if it names a different piece or you are unsure, send nothing and post your concern in chat instead of acting on it, since a capture, a threat, or a half-remembered plan is never enough reason to move.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
